ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Financial Transaction Reports Act (Act No. 6516, Jul. 24, 2001, as comprehensively amended by Act No. 10618, Dec. 28, 2010); Enforcement Decree of the Financial Transaction Reports Act (Presidential Decree No. 22914, Jun. 24, 2011, as amended); Real Name Financial Transactions and Confidentiality Act (Act No. 6866, Dec. 30, 2002, as amended); Act on the Regulation and Punishment of Criminal Proceeds Concealment (Act No. 10329, Jun. 4, 2010, as amended); Commercial Act (Act No. 1000, Dec. 20, 1962, as amended, particularly Articles 289, 317 and 544); and AML/CFT supervisory guidance and public notices issued by the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU) and the Financial Services Commission.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation (Certificate of Corporate Registration Records)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Commercial Registration Court of the district in which the registered office is located, under the Supreme Court of Korea
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For use in an Apostille Convention member state: (1) notarize the certificate before a Korean notary public; (2) obtain an Apostille from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea. For use in a non-member state: (1) notarize; (2) authenticate the certificate at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs; (3) obtain Consular Legalization from the competent consulate or embassy of the destination state in the Republic of Korea. The Apostille and Consular Legalization paths are mutually exclusive and must never be chained sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Certificate of No Unpaid Taxes / Tax Compliance)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National Tax Service of the Republic of Korea (competent District Tax Office)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For Apostille Convention destination states: (1) notarize the Korean-issued tax certificate; (2) secure a Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs Apostille. For non-member states: (1) notarize; (2) MOFA authentication; (3) destination-state consulate or embassy Legalization. Do not combine the two authentication paths.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney (authorizing the formation agent and local representative)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors of the Chusik Hoesa, notarized by a Korean notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille approach for member states: Korean notarial act followed by MOFA Apostille. Consular approach for non-member states: Korean notarial act followed by MOFA authentication and consular legalization by the destination state. The chosen path is exclusive and non-sequential.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association (Certified Copy as Filed with the Commercial Registration Court)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Initial shareholders and incorporators; filed with and certified by the Commercial Registration Court
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For member states: notarization of the certified copy and MOFA Apostille. For non-member states: notarization, MOFA authentication, and consular legalization by the destination state. Never apply both legalization routes to the same document.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter (Corporate Account Good Standing and Verification of Beneficial Owner)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: A commercial bank domiciled in the Republic of Korea and licensed by the Financial Services Commission (e.g., Kookmin, Shinhan, Hana, Woori Bank)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For member states: bank red-flag statement and signatory verification notarized, then MOFA Apostille. For non-member states: notarization, MOFA authentication, and destination-state consular legalization. The two pathways are parallel and mutually exclusive.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Before onboarding any director, shareholder, officer, or ultimate beneficial owner, the corporate service provider must screen the subject against the Consolidated United Nations Security Council Sanctions List and relevant UN Resolutions; the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List and country-by-country sanctions programs; the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List; the Republic of Korea domestic sanctions list administered by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the Financial Services Commission; KoFIU public advisories concerning money laundering and terrorism financing risks; global PEP databases covering immediate family and close associates; and adverse media and enforcement records. Screening must be repeated at beneficial-ownership changes of 25% or more, at corporate bank account opening, at large or unusual cross-border payment initiation, and upon any change of registered office or payment rails. All screening results, sanctions hits, PEP flags, and clearance decisions must be documented and retained for not less than five years after the end of the business relationship pursuant to the Financial Transaction Reports Act and its Enforcement Decree.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Internet Registration Office (I-RO) of the Supreme Court of Korea (www.iro.go.kr), together with the National Tax Service HomeTax portal (www.hometax.go.kr) for business registration name confirmation.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The Chusik Hoesa trade name must be registered in Hangul. An optional concurrently used English name must be a faithful phonetic transliteration of the registered Hangul name in accordance with the Revised Romanization system, or a recognized transliteration adopted in the articles of association. The four-tier naming convention comprises: (1) the legal entity suffix 'Chusik Hoesa'; (2) a distinctive proprietary trade name; (3) a business purpose clause; and (4) a designation of the registered office. Identical or confusingly similar names already registered in the same registry court are prohibited.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the registry court rejects a name, the incorporator must file a written objection with the district court registration office within two weeks from receipt of the rejection notice, explaining the name's inherent distinctiveness and absence of consumer confusion. Upon denial of the objection, an immediate appeal (jaegyeong) to the Seoul High Court must be lodged within one week under the Non-Contentious Case Litigation Procedure Act. Before resubmitting, the applicant must obtain the prior ministerial approval required for any sensitive token, and may refresh the name by refiling through the I-RO portal after the 30-day clearance window expires.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual offices and commercial mailboxes are not acceptable as the sole registered office of a Chusik Hoesa for the online retail of hydroponics and garden equipment. The National Tax Service and commercial banks require a physical operating address evidenced by a lease or ownership certificate, utility bills in the company name, and, in practice, a visible business presence. Local district tax offices may invalidate the business registration or reject VAT zero-rating and export claims if the address is merely a virtual mailbox, and banks will refuse corporate account onboarding without a physical address matching the business registration.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist for unannounced inspections: (1) existence of a physical office with company signage and access; (2) staff or authorized personnel present; (3) utility and internet bills in the company name; (4) lease agreement and deposit payment records; (5) actual inventory or operational equipment for e-commerce; (6) compliance with business registration certificate posting. Quantified risk: approximately 30% within the first 12 months for a new online retail company; the risk increases to 65% if a virtual office or commercial mailbox is detected, if immediate large export invoices are presented, or if third-party reports indicate absence from the registered address.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea, principally Articles 288 through 318 governing the formation of a Chusik Hoesa (stock corporation), specifically Article 289 (contents of articles of incorporation), Article 295 (subscription of shares), Article 296 (payment of subscription price), Article 306 (registration of incorporation), Article 317 (effect of incorporation registration), and Article 383 (board of directors organization); supplemented by the Commercial Registration Rules, the Presidential Decree on Commercial Registration, and the Enforcement Decree of the Act on Consumer Protection in Electronic Commerce.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Registration Division, Registration Office of the District Court having territorial jurisdiction over the company's registered office; for a Seoul registered office, the Seoul Central District Court Registration Office, administered under the supervision of the Supreme Court of Korea.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized Articles of Incorporation together with the Incorporation Registration Application prescribed by the Commercial Registration Rules, presented with the first board resolution, officers' acceptances, subscription payment certificate, and seal registration forms.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is imposed on a Chusik Hoesa under Korean law. The promoters may lawfully state a zero or de minimis initial paid-in capital in the articles, provided that the total issue price of all subscribed shares is fully paid into a Korean licensed bank subscription account established for the company in formation. That account is statutorily blocked and may not be withdrawn until the incorporation registration is completed. There is no government-required escrow separate from this bank deposit regime; after registration, the blocked amount becomes the company's available paid-in capital.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS RESOLUTION OF [●] CHUSIK HOESA

RESOLVED, that the Company, formed under the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea, hereby authorizes and ratifies the articles of incorporation as notarized on [date], including the corporate name [●] Chusik Hoesa and the registered office at [full address], Republic of Korea. The board confirms that the authorized share capital and issued shares have been established as follows: the Company shall issue a total of [number] ordinary shares, par value KRW [●], all of which have been validly subscribed for at an aggregate subscription price of KRW [●], and that such aggregate price has been deposited into the statutory pre-incorporation bank account at [bank], account number [●]. The board ratifies the stock subscription arrangements and directs that share certificates be executed and delivered to the subscribers immediately after the incorporation registration is completed.

RESOLVED FURTHER, that the board authorizes and instructs [bank] to honor all checks, wire transfers, withdrawal orders, letters of credit, electronic banking instructions, and any other transactions of the Company's accounts, provided that such instructions are signed, or contain the dual-control signatures when required, by any of the following authorized signatories: [name], [position]; [name], [position]. Any account opened for the Company prior to incorporation registration is adopted as a corporate account of the Company.

RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office of the Company is adopted and fixed as [full address], Republic of Korea, and that this office shall be the Company's legal seat, principal place of business, location of statutory registers and corporate seal, and address for service of legal process.

RESOLVED FURTHER, that the board appoints the following statutory officers: (a) [name] as Director and Chief Executive Officer; (b) [name] as Director and Corporate Secretary; and (c) [name] as Auditor, if an auditor is required or if the Company has not validly waived audit under applicable Korean law. Each officer shall hold office until a successor is duly elected and qualified and may perform all acts incidental to the operation of the Company, including executing filings with the Commercial Registry, the National Tax Service, the local municipal e-commerce seller reporting office, and any applicable licensing authority.

RESOLVED FURTHER, that the corporate seal of the Company, an impression of which is attached to these minutes as Exhibit C, shall be affixed to all share certificates, contracts, banking forms, and registration documents only upon the board's written authorization. The Corporate Secretary is directed to maintain the seal under dual custody and to issue certified copies of this resolution to banks, government registries, and other official bodies as necessary.

RESOLVED FURTHER, that the officers are authorized to pay all incorporation fees, registration taxes, notary fees, and professional fees, and to make all applications, declarations, and affidavits required to complete the incorporation registration, obtain a business registration certificate, and satisfy the notification requirements of the Act on Consumer Protection in Electronic Commerce.

RESOLVED FINALLY, that this resolution may be executed in counterparts and shall be effective as of the date it is signed. Unless earlier revoked, this resolution shall continue until the first annual general meeting of shareholders or until superseded by a subsequent board resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft, Notarize, and Seal the Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A notary public licensed by the Ministry of Justice of the Republic of Korea sitting within the district of the intended registered office; the same notarized articles will later be presented to the District Court Commercial Registry.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The promoters shall convene an inaugural organizational meeting, adopt a written resolution approving the articles of incorporation, and confirm the business purpose as online retail and e-commerce supply of home hydroponics and gardening equipment (ISIC 4791). The Korean-language articles must state the corporate name, business object, total authorized shares, par value, number of subscription shares, registered office address, and the names of the initial directors and auditor. The draft articles must be submitted to a notary public together with the organizational meeting resolution. Each promoter shall sign and seal the articles in the notary's presence, and the notary shall issue a notarial certificate. The notarized articles form the organic charter of the company and may not be altered after subscription except by a special shareholders' resolution. The corporate seal specimen and personal seal certificates required for registration should be prepared at the same time.
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Incorporation
Notarized minutes of the preparatory organizational meeting
Personal seal certificate and photo identification of each promoter
Corporate seal specimen or proposed company seal imprint
Written consent to appointment of each initial director and auditor
Power of attorney if any promoter is represented by an agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or registry raises a formal objection to the articles, the promoters must pass a corrective resolution, re-notarize the amended articles, and resubmit the complete package. A registry suspension notice must be cured within the court's stated correction period. If the matter is finally rejected, the promoters may file a new application or bring an immediate appeal against the registration judge's order; any defective clauses must be redrafted and re-notarized before resubmission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit Share Subscription Price into a Blocked Bank Account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: The corporate banking division of a Korean licensed commercial bank selected by the board, with the transaction evidenced by the bank's certificate of deposit of subscription moneys.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Under Article 296 of the Commercial Act, the aggregate subscription price for all promoters' shares must be paid into a Korean financial institution before the incorporation registration application is filed. The promoter must open a restricted subscription deposit account in the name of the company in formation or the promoter, as approved by the bank; deposit the full subscription amount; and obtain the bank's certificate or deposit receipt identifying the depositor, amount, purpose, and date. The account must remain blocked until the company's incorporation registration is entered and the bank receives a certified corporate registration extract. Any in-kind contribution requires special authorization in the articles and, where required, appraisal by a court-appointed examiner. Payment must be made in Korean won unless the bank expressly permits foreign currency treatment consistent with the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act.
required_dossiers: Promoter identification and personal seal certificates
Notarized articles of incorporation
Pre-incorporation bank account application and signature forms
Source-of-funds documentation for anti-money-laundering verification
Preparatory meeting resolution authorizing the bank and signatories
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank rejects the deposit due to anti-money-laundering or know-your-customer concerns, corrected identification, source-of-funds evidence, or an amended board resolution must be supplied. If the deposit certificate contains an incorrect name or amount, request a written correction or a refund and redeposit, and ensure that the statutory blockage is not released before incorporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Apply for Incorporation Registration at the District Court Commercial Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registration Office of the District Court with jurisdiction over the registered office address; for Seoul, the Seoul Central District Court Registration Office, acting through a registration judge or delegated judicial registrar.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within two weeks after the share subscription payment is completed, the promoters or their legal representative must file the incorporation registration application with the competent court. The application must state the corporate object, name, share capital, registered office, directors, auditors, and representation authority, and must attach the notarized articles, share subscription payment certificate, directors' written acceptances, lease or ownership evidence of the registered office, and corporate seal registration form. The registrar verifies statutory compliance and, if satisfied, enters the company into the commercial register and issues a corporate registration certificate and certified extract. The company acquires legal personality only upon this entry. After registration, the registry transmits the registration data to the National Tax Service and the relevant local government through the integrated administrative information system. Registration taxes and fees are assessed and collected at the court window or through the online e-Register System based on the declared paid-in capital.
required_dossiers: Completed incorporation registration application
Notarized articles of incorporation
Certificate of deposit of the subscription price
Written acceptance of office by each director and auditor
Minutes of the organizational meeting and first board resolution
Evidence of registered office address or lease
Corporate seal registration application
Power of attorney if submitted through a legal agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar issues a correction order, submit supplementary documents or amended forms within the prescribed period. If the application is suspended or rejected, the applicants may file an immediate appeal under the Non-Contentious Case Litigation Act. If rejection is based on invalid articles, revise the articles by notarization and file a fresh application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register for Corporate Business and E-Commerce Seller Reporting
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service through the local District Tax Office and the HOMETAX online portal; separately, the competent local municipal government (Si/Gun/Gu) receives the communications-sales seller notification under the Act on Consumer Protection in Electronic Commerce, with the Korea Fair Trade Commission as the supervising authority.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within twenty days after incorporation registration, the company must apply for a business registration certificate with the district tax office having jurisdiction over the registered office, listing the value-added-tax-registered business activity as the online sale of home hydroponics and gardening equipment. The application must include the corporate name, business address, representative director, telephone, email, and e-commerce activity code. The National Tax Service will issue the business registration certificate and corporate tax identification number. Because the company will sell to consumers over the internet under ISIC 4791, it must also file the communications-sales seller notification with the competent local authority within the statutory period, providing seller identity, address, contact details, and the online sales platform information. These two filings are distinct: the NTS business registration is tax compliance, while the local municipality notification is the consumer-protection registration prerequisite for lawful online trading.
required_dossiers: Certified corporate registration extract
Business registration application (HOMETAX)
Corporate seal certificate and seal specimen
Representative director's identification
Lease contract or address proof for the registered office
Board resolution appointing the responsible e-commerce reporting officer
Bank account certificate or provisional account details
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office queries the application, correct the business address, owner information, or activity classification and re-file through HOMETAX. If the municipality rejects the communications-sales notification, submit a revised business scope statement or an express confirmation that the company is not engaged in manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing. Administrative appeals to the National Tax Tribunal or local government review are available if the denial is not cured.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open Operational Bank Account, Issue Share Certificates, and Formalize Statutory Books
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: The licensed commercial bank designated by the board; the corporate secretary and legal representative complete the bank KYC process and the shareholders' register is maintained at the registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the business registration certificate and corporate registration extract, the company shall open its operational corporate bank account at the designated branch by presenting the corporate registration extract, business registration certificate, corporate seal certificate, and board resolution identifying authorized signatories. The bank will conduct know-your-customer and beneficial-ownership verification, and signature cards will be lodged. Simultaneously, the board shall issue physical share certificates to each subscriber, record all subscribers in the shareholders' register, and prepare the statutory books, including the directors' register, audit register if applicable, minutes book, and seal custody ledger. The corporate seal must be maintained under dual control and used only with an internal written authorization form. The share certificates and statutory registers must be available for inspection by shareholders and tax authorities at the registered office.
required_dossiers: Corporate registration extract
Business registration certificate
Corporate seal certificate and seal specimen
Board resolution on bank signatories and capital verification
Passport or national identification of each director and beneficial owner
Share subscription list and payment receipts
Certified copy of the first board resolution for the bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank imposes enhanced due diligence, provide the requested source-of-funds evidence, entity ownership structure, and a board resolution confirming the beneficial owner. If share certificate issuance is contested, record the objection in the minutes and obtain a corrective board resolution. Any incidence of forged seal or unauthorized use must be remedied by filing a seal declaration with the district court and notifying the bank immediately.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - no ISIC 1xxx/2xxx/3xxx/4xxx manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing establishment is being formed; the registered activity is ISIC 4791 online retail of home hydroponics and gardening equipment.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable - no manufacturing plant license, warehouse facility permit, assembly line authorization, or industrial operating permit is required. The company must maintain the general e-commerce seller report described in the SOP, but that is a consumer-protection notification, not an industrial operating license.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment of the Republic of Korea / Not Applicable
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable; the company has no regulated point-source wastewater discharge, volatile organic compound emission, or hazardous waste generation from the registered online-retail office. If the company later establishes warehousing with refrigeration equipment, assembly work, or any chemical or manufacturing process, an Environmental Impact Assessment screening or consultation will be required under the Environmental Impact Assessment Act, and thresholds under the Clean Air Conservation Act and the Water Environment Conservation Act will need to be recertified.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable for the pure online-retail operation; the registered office is an office occupancy subject to the ordinary Building Act requirements for emergency exits, fire extinguishers, and electrical safety compliance under the Korea Electrical Safety Corporation. No Civil Defense fire safety permit is required unless the company subsequently holds a producing, warehouse, assembly, or industrial license that requires fire inspection under the Fire Safety and Life Safety Code.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS); online portal: HomeTax (hometax.go.kr). Korea Customs Service (KCS); UNI-PASS portal (unipass.customs.go.kr).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Korean Chusik Hoesa must apply for Business Operator Registration with the competent tax office through HomeTax within 20 days of business commencement, furnishing the corporate registration certificate, articles of incorporation, evidence of the registered place of business, representative identity document, and power of attorney; NTS then issues a 10-digit Business Registration Number. A foreign non-resident entity with no Korean place of business that is required to account for Korean VAT must appoint a Korean tax representative and file a Foreign Business Operator Registration through the HomeTax foreign operator e-service, attaching the home-country corporate registration certificate, articles or charter, identity/passport of the representative, and the signed Korean tax representative appointment; NTS issues a Foreign Business Operator Registration Number used for VAT returns and e-tax invoices.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation (the Chusik Hoesa is treated as a domestic corporation taxable on worldwide income under the Corporate Tax Act; pass-through is not available).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None available for entity classification; no U.S.-style check-the-box election. A qualifying wholly-owned Korean group may elect to file a consolidated corporate tax base under the Corporate Tax Act; a small enterprise may elect simplified VAT treatment when annual taxable turnover is below KRW 80,000,000; an exporter may elect to claim zero-rated VAT refunds in the periodic VAT return.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: KRW 0 (no turnover threshold; all Korean business operators must register under the Value-Added Tax Act. Simplified taxable person classification applies when annual tax-inclusive turnover is below KRW 80,000,000, but registration remains mandatory).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Electronic tax invoices are mandatory for all registered businesses. The electronic tax invoice must be transmitted in HomeTax XML format, either directly through the HomeTax portal or via an approved ERP/API integration, to the National Tax Service by the end of the day following issuance. Korea does not operate a real-time fiscal pre-clearance or digital stamping model; anti-fraud control is achieved through the central e-tax invoice registry, cash receipts for simplified B2C sales, six-monthly VAT returns, and automated cross-checks with KCS customs declarations and foreign exchange transaction records.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Article 21 of the Value-Added Tax Act, physical export of goods to a foreign country qualifies for the 0% rate. For the hydroponics e-commerce scope, the seller must prove that the goods left Korea under a valid export customs declaration, the overseas purchaser is a non-resident, consideration is payable in foreign currency, and export proceeds are repatriated through a Korean foreign exchange bank. Offshore digital services and other supplies performed outside Korea for a non-resident are similarly zero-rated when actually rendered abroad and paid for in foreign exchange. The 0% rate is claimed on the VAT return and documentary evidence must be retained.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: KCS Export Declaration and Export Clearance Certificate issued through UNI-PASS
Ocean Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical departure from Korea
Foreign Exchange Purchase Receipt / Inward Remittance Evidence issued by a Korean foreign exchange bank showing receipt of export proceeds from the overseas purchaser
Purchase Order / Overseas Sales Contract or online marketplace settlement report
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Zero-rating claims are audited through the NTS-KCS interlock: the VAT return is matched with UNI-PASS export clearance data, transport documents, and the exporter's foreign exchange bank collection records. A claim is disallowed or clawed back if the export declaration is cancelled, goods are re-imported or diverted to domestic consumption, no bankable proof of receipt of foreign sales proceeds exists within the statutory 18-month (540-day) period from export declaration unless an extension is granted, or documents are forged. Consequences include reassessment of unpaid VAT at 10%, additional tax for unfaithful returns and tax invoice violations, statutory interest on the understated position, recovery of refunds already paid with surcharge, and criminal referral under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act for fraudulent evasion.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK), with foreign exchange administration delegated to the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF), and enforcement shared with the Korea Customs Service (KCS) and designated foreign exchange banks; the BOK operates the foreign exchange information system and official reserves framework.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea operates a liberalised current account under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act; bona fide trade, service, and dividend remittance flows can be settled in freely convertible foreign currency through a designated foreign exchange bank with minimal documentary reporting. The Korean won is not a freely internationally traded reserve currency but is market convertible subject to a managed floating regime and strict capital-account gatekeeping. Capital contributions, equity subscriptions, and cross-border loans require FIPA foreign-investment notification, bank registration, and periodic reports; they cannot be received without an underlying corporate or trade transaction. Profit remittances are lawful after corporate audit and statutory reserve retention, but the paying bank requires the board dividend resolution, audited financial statements, tax withholding certificates, and a Foreign Exchange Information System report. No mandatory export surrender ratio applies to Korean export receipts; exporters may park proceeds in foreign currency accounts. However, all cross-border settlement in Korea must be supported by real underlying business, and foreign exchange banks have discretion to reject transactions that appear speculative or inconsistent with the registered ISIC 4791 e-commerce business.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and KCS foreign exchange regulations, export proceeds must be collected within 18 months from the date of export declaration unless an extended collection period is approved by the designated foreign exchange bank. There is no fixed mandatory conversion ratio into KRW; Korean exporters may retain export settlement in approved foreign currency accounts and sell only the amount needed for KRW operating liquidity. The bank must be given the export declaration number and collection evidence, and any uncollected overdue balance must be reported with a reason through the foreign exchange information system.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: FDI Capital Contribution Account and KRW Operational Current Account
FDI Capital Contribution Account and Foreign Currency Corporate Savings Account
FDI Capital Contribution Account and Basic Operational KRW Account
FDI Capital Contribution Account and Operational Dual-Currency Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Foreign fintech EMIs are legally barred from serving as the principal bank treasury in Korea. Only institutions licensed under the Banking Act or the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act can open an onshore KRW corporate settlement account; Korea does not use IBANs, and an offshore EMI cannot generate a locally valid Korean account. Stripe and PayPal remain permissible as front-end online acquiring/payment gateway rails, but all settlement proceeds must be auto-swept to a licensed Korean bank account. Feasibility rating: Low-to-zero for treasury, liquidity, and FX clearing; High for card acquisition and customer checkout purposes only.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Initial corporate account opening in Korea requires physical presence of the representative statutory director or a director with signatory authority at the branch; an Alien Registration Card (ARC) or foreigner registration certificate is required for a non-Korean director. Remote notarised powers of attorney are not accepted as a substitute for first-time customer due diligence. The bank may accept a video interview only after the director has already registered in Korea; the final account mandate must still be executed in the branch or through an approved electronic certificate tied to the ARC.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Hydroponics and garden equipment e-commerce is mischaracterised as a grey-market channel for controlled-substance paraphernalia; the wide ISIC 4791 online retail category creates revenue narrative uncertainty for the bank's reputational risk committee.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Official certificate of business registration designated as online retail of home gardening and hydroponics equipment; detailed product and HS classification list proving the goods are concrete garden equipment, nutrient solutions, LED lighting, and irrigation hardware; supplier master contracts and purchase invoices; Stripe/PayPal merchant category codes and rejection rates; a board-approved sales policy expressly excluding products intended for illegal drug production; and a certified Korean/English translation of the business scope and e-commerce platform terms.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound foreign shareholder capital injection from a low-registry or high-surveillance jurisdiction cannot be validated as clean equity because the Chusik Hoesa has no statutory minimum capital and the investor may be using the operating entity as a bridge for third-party funds.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified passport or corporate registry evidence of the shareholder and all UBOs; two years of audited financial statements or tax returns for the investor; a bank reference from the remitting foreign bank confirming the credit origin; FIPA foreign investment notification receipt from KOTRA or the designated bank; signed board resolution approving the capital increase; and a source-of-wealth narrative supported by asset and income records.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: PayPal and Stripe batch payouts commingle hundreds of end-customer payments and can mask third-party money laundering, particularly when the same online shop sells consumable nutrient products with repeat subscriptions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete merchant settlement reports from Stripe and PayPal with raw order IDs, gross sales, fees, refunds, and net payout values; monthly platform statements; a reconciliation ledger matching each settlement batch to identifiable customers and orders; procedures for refund and chargeback handling; and the company's AML/CFT customer screening policy for high-risk addresses or repeated cash-equivalent prepayment patterns.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-based money laundering is suspected when import disbursements are made to non-supplier beneficiaries or through trade intermediaries without proof that the goods entered Korea and correspond to physical inventory.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Commercial invoices, packing lists, bills of lading or air waybills, Korean Customs import declarations, and customs duty and tax receipts; original supplier sourcing contracts; a written explanation and legal reason for any third-party payment intermediary; independent pricing evidence or quoted catalogue valuation to support arm's-length pricing; and a director's declaration confirming that the imported goods are the same physical products sold through the online catalogue.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The foreign shareholder sends an SWIFT MT103 from a foreign financial institution to the Korean bank's correspondent account, payable to the Chusik Hoesa's FDI capital contribution account. The payment narrative must state 'Equity contribution for paid-in capital under FIPA' and the bank will assign a foreign exchange purpose code for inward foreign investment in the Foreign Exchange Information System. After credit, the bank issues a foreign exchange and foreign investment certificate; the company then instructs an external Korean auditor or CPA to verify paid-in capital under the Commercial Act, amends the commercial registry, and files the FIPA post-investment report with KOTRA. No KRW remittance should be used unless the bank has pre-approved the use of Korean won in a designated foreign direct investment settlement scheme.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For importing garden hydroponics equipment, the company can use a SWIFT MT103 for T/T open-account payments, an irrevocable sight letter of credit (L/C) for large purchase orders, or documentary collections (D/P and D/A) for established supplier lines. Every disbursement must reference the Korean Customs import declaration and the underlying supplier invoice, with the bank mapping the transaction to an outbound goods-import purpose code. Stripe and PayPal must not be used for supplier payments; those platforms are only payment acceptance rails, and their settlement funds are swept to the Korean bank before any KRW or foreign currency disbursement is made.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Delivered onshore KRW/USD or KRW/CNH forward contracts booked with a designated foreign exchange bank, limited to the value of evidenced import payables or export receivables with a maximum maturity aligned to the underlying trade cycle.

Cross-currency swaps are permitted only for hedging real trade or investment principal and interest obligations, and they require bank treasury credit approval plus a clear link to the Chusik Hoesa's balance-sheet exposure; uncovered or speculative swaps are prohibited.

Offshore KRW non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are generally not usable by the domestic operating entity; the non-resident shareholder may hedge its KRW equity exposure through bank-approved NDF or currency derivatives only when real demand is demonstrated and the transaction is reported under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return with tax-reconciliation schedules, financial statements and corporate income tax payment confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) - competent district tax office of the registered head office via HomeTax electronic filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before March 31 immediately following a December 31 fiscal year-end; for a non-calendar fiscal year, by the last day of the third month after the fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Under-reported or unreported corporate income tax attracts 20% surtax or 40% in fraudulent/aggravated cases, plus a statutory daily late-payment interest charge until paid; prolonged non-filing permits official NTS assessment, enforcement seizure of assets, and cancellation of the business registration after administrative notice.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local corporate income tax surcharge return and payment on the corporate income tax base allocated to the head-office locality
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Competent city/county local government tax office (Korea Local Tax Administration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same date as the national corporate income tax filing: by March 31 for a December 31 fiscal year-end, or by the last day of the third month after the fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Local corporate income tax delinquency triggers 20% surtax on unfiled or underpaid local tax, 40% in fraudulent cases, daily late-payment interest, and local-government collection measures including seizure of bank accounts and cancellation of the business registration certificate.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Semi-annual value-added tax returns covering e-commerce sales of hydroponics and gardening equipment supplied by the Chusik Hoesa
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: First VAT period January 1 - June 30 due July 25; second VAT period July 1 - December 31 due January 25 of the next calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or under-declaring VAT liability subjects the company to 20% additional tax (40% for dishonest/receipt-fabrication cases) plus statutory daily late-payment interest; repeated non-filing can lead to tax assessment, asset seizure, and administrative cancellation of the business registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Ordinary annual general meeting of shareholders including presentation and approval of financial statements, dividend resolution, and appointment or reappointment of directors and statutory auditor
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: No government authority receives the meeting itself; notice is issued to shareholders and approved minutes are kept in the company minute book at the registered office for inspection by NTS or court officers upon request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the close of each fiscal year, i.e., by June 30 for a December 31 fiscal year; share-certificate holders must be notified at least 14 days before the meeting date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to convene the annual meeting may attract administrative fines up to KRW 5,000,000 under the Commercial Act, invalidates certain corporate resolutions for lack of approval, and exposes the board to a shareholder-applied court order to convene an extraordinary meeting.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Commercial registry filings for annual reappointment or resignation of directors, statutory auditors, registered office moves, or other registrable corporate changes approved at the annual meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Registration Court of the district court having jurisdiction over the registered head office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 14 days from the date of the change, normally from the annual general meeting or board resolution date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late registration attracts an administrative fine of up to KRW 5,000,000 and, until registered, the newly appointed director or changed corporate details cannot be asserted against a good-faith third party; long-term failure to maintain registrable information can support a court-initiated dissolution or removal action for non-compliant stock corporations.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Independent certified CPA audit report, audited financial statements and external-auditor filings for Chusik Hoesa entities that meet the statutory mandatory audit thresholds
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) through its DART electronic disclosure system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a December 31 year-end, no later than April 30 following the fiscal year-end and, in all cases, within two weeks after the ordinary annual general meeting at which the audited financial statements are approved
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to appoint an external auditor or file the statutory audit report with the FSS can result in corrective orders, administrative fines, referral to public prosecution, suspension of the auditor registration, and disqualification of the company from certain public-market benefits.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual foreign investment enterprise status report including ultimate beneficial owner and capital-movement details for any non-resident shareholder holding a reportable foreign investment in the Chusik Hoesa
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE) through Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA) or the designated foreign-exchange bank with which the foreign investment is registered, as applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 90 days after the close of the fiscal year, i.e., by March 31 for a December 31 fiscal year-end; reportable shareholding changes must also be notified within 30 days of the transfer
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure or delay in reporting may attract administrative fines under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, loss of foreign investment protection and incentive benefits, restriction on dividend remittances, and inability to rely on the foreign investment registration for subsequent capital transactions.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Chusik Hoesa is mandatorily subject to an independent certified public accountant audit under the Act on External Audit and Governance of Stock Companies if (i) total assets at the fiscal year-end exceed KRW 12,000,000,000 (approx USD 9.1 million); (ii) annual revenue exceeds KRW 100,000,000,000 (approx USD 76 million); (iii) the average workforce exceeds 300 employees; (iv) the company is a listed issuer or an FSS-designated public-interest entity, irrespective of size; or (v) the company meets the consolidated size tests in the Enforcement Decree of the External Audit Act. A small garden-technology e-commerce corporation below all thresholds is audit-exempt unless shareholders holding at least 5% of the voting shares validly request an extraordinary audit or the company voluntarily appoints a certified auditor.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Statutory audit reports of mandatory-audit entities are prepared under K-IFRS (Korean International Financial Reporting Standards as endorsed by the Korean Accounting Standards Board). Eligible non-public small and medium enterprises below the K-IFRS mandate may apply Korean GAAP for non-public entities. Regardless of framework, financial statements must be prepared in accordance with the External Audit Act, the Commercial Act accounting provisions, and the Korean Accounting Standards Board statements, and the auditor must be a licensed Korean CPA registered with the Financial Supervisory Service.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: South Korea does not operate a separate annual UBO return for an ordinary non-listed Chusik Hoesa. Beneficial ownership is instead evidenced by the statutory Register of Members, the share-transfer records, and the foreign investment register: a share transfer must be recorded in the Register of Members within 30 days of transfer notice to be effective against the company; director and statutory auditor changes must be filed with the Commercial Registration Court within 14 days; and a non-resident beneficial holder of at least 10% of the share capital must be captured in the annual foreign investment enterprise status report filed within 90 days of the fiscal year-end. The registered office must maintain the statutory registers on site in a form available for inspection by an NTS auditor, a court-appointed inspector, or the external auditor during annual register audits.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Shares and Share Certificates
Minute Book of board of directors' meetings

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 450 to USD 1,800 per year depending on Seoul/Metro location, registered-office services, mail forwarding, and company secretarial support
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 0 for a micro-cap or small e-commerce Chusik Hoesa below all statutory audit thresholds; approximately USD 8,000 to USD 25,000 for an audit-target entity with online retail transaction sets and cross-border receipts.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 22% (for taxable income exceeding KRW 20 billion; 10% below KRW 200 million; 20% from KRW 200 million to KRW 20 billion)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: R&D tax credit equal to up to 25%-50% of qualifying R&D expenditure subject to statutory ceilings; foreign investment tax incentives under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act for eligible high-tech and export businesses located in Free Economic Zones; income tax exemption/reduction for venture SMEs under the Restriction of Special Taxation Act, and temporary investment tax credits; no patent box regime.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Korean Corporate Tax Return (法人稅課稅標準及稅額申告書) filed through the National Tax Service HomeTax electronic portal (www.hometax.go.kr), form classification: Standard Corporate Tax Return for General Enterprises (Form A/B).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (fiscal-year basis, with half-year preliminary corporate tax payments due by the end of the sixth month of the fiscal period).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within three months from the end of the fiscal year; for a December 31 year-end the filing deadline is March 31; up to one additional month extension if financial statements are certified by independent auditors.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: 甲 1 - Corporation Name, Business Registration Number, Foreign Investment Status
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Basic identification data of the Chusik Hoesa: legal name, business registration number, principal place of business, industry code (ISIC 4791), and fiscal year-end date.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Insert the foreign investment registration reference and the percentage of non-resident shareholding. Attach foreign capital report details to substantiate inflow of paid-in capital from foreign owners. Failure to declare foreign ownership may result in an incorrect return penalty and may invalidate treaty benefits claimed on subsequent dividend distributions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: 甲 3 - Tax Base Computation: Gross Income less Deductible Expenses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report worldwide gross revenue from online retail sales of garden hydroponics equipment, cost of sales, selling, general and administrative expenses, and deductible business costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For cross-border related-party purchases, import duties, freight, and commissions, annotate the arm's length basis in the supplementary TP schedules. Strictly disallow non-deductible expense items such as corporate income tax and fines. Maintain contemporaneous e-commerce transaction records, merchant statements from Stripe and PayPal, and customer invoice records to avoid forensic reconstruction of income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: 乙 2 - Adjustments: Special Reserves, Non-deductible Items, and Tax-Exempt Income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Line adjustments applied to statutory accounting profit to arrive at taxable income, including special reserves for technology development, pending litigations, and foreign exchange fluctuations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Where the Korean entity transacts with any non-resident related party, report any transfer pricing adjustments (positive or negative) in the attached international transaction reconciliation statement. Ensure that any deemed dividend from an adjustment is reflected in the corporate income tax base and that the relevant compensating entries are traceable in the contemporaneous documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: 丁 5 - Foreign Tax Credit and Foreign Income Exemption
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of foreign income taxes paid by the Korean corporation on income sourced outside Korea and creditable against Korean corporate income tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide official foreign tax assessment notices or Local Tax payment receipts for any branch profits, warehouse inventory sale margins, or overseas digital platform levies. Convert foreign taxes at the spot exchange rate used in the tax invoice. Do not claim a tax credit for amounts for which a treaty exemption has already been obtained. Suspected double-dipping may trigger a criminal audit.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing or non-filing of Corporate Tax Return triggers an additional 20% of the unpaid tax for unfaithful return, plus 0.022% daily interest from due date to payment date; wilful omission of taxable sales or fraudulent returns are subject to 30% supplementary tax, a further 20% of underreporting if report is materially false, and criminal referral for tax evasion with imprisonment up to 3 years and fine up to 3 times the evaded tax.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% (corporate tax withholding rate 20% under Article 98 of the Corporate Tax Act plus 2% local income tax surcharge under the Local Tax Act) on outbound dividends paid to non-resident shareholders, including deemed dividends.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a reduced dividend rate under an applicable Double Tax Treaty (DTA), the non-resident shareholder must (1) obtain and provide to the Korean payer a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by its residence country in the current tax year; (2) deliver a fully executed beneficial ownership declaration (Form-application for Treaty-Based Tax Exemption/Reduction) disclosing the ultimate beneficial owner and absence of conduit arrangements; (3) submit these documents before payment or by the due date of the withholding return, otherwise the 22% statutory WHT applies. If the documents are provided late, the recipient may file a refund claim with the Korean tax authority within five years of filing date; all substantiation must be supported by notarised translations for non-English documents.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rates: interest 22% (20% national + 2% local surcharge); royalties 22% (same composition). Under most Korean DTAs the treaty rates are: interest 10% (0-10% for certain bank loans), royalties 10% for literature and cultural royalties and up to 15% for industrial, commercial, or scientific equipment; royalties for patents, know-how and software licenses commonly capped at 10%; the treaty rate applies only if the recipient is the beneficial owner.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File preparation threshold:KRW 10,000,000,000 of international related-party transactions for immediately preceding fiscal year; Master File threshold: consolidated annual revenue of KRW 100,000,000,000 or more and international related-party transaction amount of KRW 10,000,000,000 or more; simplified documents may be required for smaller taxpayers under Notice 2022-18.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea does not impose a separate Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) code like UAE; however, the substance-over-form ground, business purpose doctrine, and the anti-abuse rules of the Restriction of International Tax Adjustment Act require that the Korean company maintain real personnel, premises, and core income-generating activities (CIGA) where decision-making on procurement, inventory ownership, marketing, and risk management occurs. A Korean e-commerce entity that operates merely as a pass-through or empty holding company can have its place of effective management shifted abroad and be denied treaty benefits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion - False Corporate Tax Return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willfully omitting overseas online sales revenue, understating PayPal/Stripe settlement proceeds, inflating cost of goods sold through fabricated purchase invoices, or using nominee shareholders to conceal offshore bank accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 138(1) of the Corporate Tax Act: imprisonment with labor not exceeding three years or a fine not exceeding three times the evaded tax; fraudulent unpaid return additional tax 30%; daily default interest 0.022%; tax delinquency listing with the National Tax Service and publication of the delinquency register.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The limited liability shield is pierced under the Commercial Act for directors who acted in bad faith or gross negligence; they are jointly and severally liable for the company's unpaid tax and penalties to the extent of damage caused; NTS imposes a departure ban (overseas travel restriction) for delinquencies exceeding KRW 50 million; criminal conviction can lead to imprisonment up to five years under the Aggravated Punishment for Specific Economic Crimes when the evasion exceeds KRW 500 million, and directors can face personal asset seizure.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Manipulation and Documentation Failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Setting the intercompany sale price of garden hydroponics equipment to a foreign related wholesaler at a manipulated margin (e.g., leaving uncovered the committed risks and valuable intangibles of the Korean seller); failing to prepare and retain the Local File / Master File; submitting a unilateral pricing arrangement without economic comparables or Chinese tax authority approval when cross-border related-party transactions exceed the KRW 10 billion threshold.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Articles 6 and 12 of Restriction of International Tax Adjustment Act: adjustment of taxable income to arm's length price; surcharge additional tax of 20% of the understated amount (30% where no disclosure); document failure penalty up to KRW 60 million; overdue interest; in severe mispricing cases, criminal referral for fraud.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly approve artificial pricing or sign false TP reports are civilly liable to the corporation and its creditors; they may be denied discharge in corporate insolvency; tax authorities may attach personal assets of directors for grossly negligent TP adjustments; blacklisting and travel ban apply for unpaid criminal fines; imprisonment up to two years can be imposed for submitting false documentation or obstruction of tax audit.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Withholding Tax Negligence / Unauthorised Treaty Relief
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends to a non-resident parent or royalty to a foreign licensor without effecting statutory 22% withholding; applying the reduced DTA rate without collecting the Tax Residency Certificate and beneficial ownership declaration; splitting privilege payments through an intermediary shell company to artificially claim a rider rate of 0% interest withholding.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 97 and Article 144 of the Corporate Tax Act: the payer is liable for the un-withheld amount, plus penalty of 10% of the un-withheld tax (20% for intentional false withholding), plus overdue interest; the un-withheld amount is denied as a deduction; local tax surcharge penalty applies at 20% of the municipal tax element.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Representative directors and financial officers are joint withholding agents; they are personally and severally liable for the remitted tax and penalties if they knowingly fail to withhold; personal bank accounts can be frozen after seven-day payment order; NTS places a departure restriction for deliberate non-withholding exceeding KRW 50 million; criminal liability under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act may impose imprisonment up to one year for wilful non-withholding.
